arabic_locator.text: وَلِهَذَا كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ يصلي الْعِيدَ  ثُمَّ يَنْحَرُ نُسُكَهُ وَيَقُولُ: "مَنْ صَلَّى صَلَاتَنَا، وَنَسَكَ نُسُكَنَا، فَقَدْ أَصَابَ النُّسُكَ. وَمَنْ نَسَكَ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ فَلَا نُسُكَ لَهُ". فَقَامَ أَبُو بُرْدَةَ بْنُ نَيَّارٍ فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي نَسكتُ شَاتِي قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ، وَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّ الْيَوْمَ يَوْمٌ يُشْتَهَى فِيهِ اللَّحْمُ. قَالَ: "شَاتُكَ شَاةُ لَحْمٍ". قَالَ: فَإِنَّ عِنْدِي عِنَاقًا هِيَ أَحَبُّ إليَّ مِنْ شَاتَيْنِ، أَفَتُجْزِئُ عَنِّي؟ قَالَ: "تُجْزِئُكَ، وَلَا تُجَزِئُ أَحَدًا بَعْدَكَ".

semantic_units.statement_en: Ibn Kathir reports that Muhammad prayed the Eid prayer and then slaughtered his sacrifice.
The quoted statement accepts sacrifice performed with the prayer and sacrifice sequence described, and denies ritual validity to sacrifice before the prayer.
Abu Burda says he slaughtered his sheep before the prayer, knowing that meat was desired that day.
The reply characterizes Abu Burda's sheep as a sheep for meat.
Abu Burda asks whether a young female goat he values more than two sheep will suffice for him.
The reply permits it for Abu Burda and states that it will not suffice for anyone after him.

fidelity_notes: Preserve alternating speakers; Abu Burda's first-person statements are not Muhammad's statements.
The final sufficiency permission is individually restricted; do not generalize it to all sacrificers.
Young female goat paraphrases anaq without inventing a precise age absent from this passage.
No complete transmitter chain or collection locator printed in this unit; no independently verified hadith number supplied.
Analytical English paraphrases; bounded English absence retained.
remaining: Resolve claim types and draft separate speaker/evidence links
Validate individually restricted exception and alternating voices before read-only CI
